texts.preamble: Manjunatha vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 20 February, 2025 Scch-21 1 Mvc No.4583/2024 Kabc0B0012962024 In The Court Of Xvii Addl. Judge, Court Of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T, Mayo Hall Unit, Bengaluru (Scch-21) Present: Vijaykumar S. Hiremath., B.Sc, L.Lb., Xvii Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T., Bengaluru. Dated this the 20th Day of February-2025 M.V.C. No.4583/2024 Petitioner/s: 1. Sri. Manjunatha
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 12.01.2024. 2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under: It is the case of the petitioner that on 12.01.2024 at about 06.00 p.m., petitioner was traveling as a pillion rider in Motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-67-E-8750 proceeding on Chikkanahalli Gate, Kolar to Bangalore NH-75 Road, Nandagudi Hobli, Hosakote, Bangalore, at that time a motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HT- 9730 ridden by its rider in a rash and negligent manner, without following any traffic rules, came at high speed and dashed against the petitioner motorcycle. Due to the forced impact, petitioner and rider fell down and sustained grievous injuries. Immediately, he was shifted to Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic & Surgical Hospital, wherein he was treated as inpatient and spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, food, transport and other charges. The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 32 years, the petitioner was working as Carpenter and earning Rs.25,000/- per month. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and lost his future income. Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle. Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest. 3. After service of notice, the respondent No.1 has appeared through his counsel and filed the written statement. Respondent No.2 has not appeared before the Court and he remained placed exparte. The respondent No.1 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition. Further this respondent admits the issuance of policy to the offending Manjunatha vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 20 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2854192/ 2 motorcycle and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy. Further this respondent submits that, the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-67-E-8750 was not holding valid and effective driving license to ride the vehicle as on the date of accident and taken 2 persons as pillion riders and caused accident by himself. It is further submitted that, accident was due to rash and negligence of both the motorcyclists and both of them involved in the accident and it is a contributory negligence. Further this respondent denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner. The petitioner colluding with the owner and police filed the false case. By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.
texts.arguments: In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M. V. Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319. 16. 19. The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses. As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble Manjunatha vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 20 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2854192/ 5 High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.
